name: Rot13withdigitreversal

description_json.name: Rot13WithDigitReversal
description_json.idea: Apply standard ROT13 to alphabetic characters (preserving case) and reverse digits (subtracting each digit from 9) to add a layer of obfuscation that remains highly intuitive and easy for language models to process accurately.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it by 13 positions: new_char = chr(((ord(char) - 65 + 13) % 26) + 65).
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it by 13 positions: new_char = chr(((ord(char) - 97 + 13) % 26) + 97).
3. If it is a digit (0-9), subtract its integer value from 9: new_char = str(9 - int(char)).
4. If it is any other character (spaces, punctuation, symbols), leave it unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it back by 13 positions (which is identical to shifting forward by 13): new_char = chr(((ord(char) - 65 + 13) % 26) + 65).
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it back by 13 positions: new_char = chr(((ord(char) - 97 + 13) % 26) + 97).
3. If it is a digit (0-9), subtract its integer value from 9: new_char = str(9 - int(char)).
4. If it is any other character, leave it unchanged.
